nodes.html: Registered Tax Agent — what we can help with
nodes.text: Registered Tax Agent — what we can help with

nodes.html: Under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009, only a registered tax (or BAS) agent can charge a fee to lodge returns or deal with the ATO on your behalf. Unregistered operators cannot legally do this — and the ATO will not deal with them. Every accountant in our network has a current TPB registration that we verify. If an agent's registration lapses, they are removed from the network.

nodes.text: How to check a tax agent's registration

nodes.html: You can verify any agent on the Tax Practitioners Board's public register at tpb.gov.au using their name or registration number. When you are matched through our service, we confirm TPB registration before the match is shown to you. You can also ask the matched firm directly for their registration number.

nodes.html: A 'tax accountant' is a job title; 'registered tax agent' is a legal authorisation. All our matched firms that lodge returns are registered tax agents — the registration is what gives them the legal right to lodge and represent you. An unregistered 'tax accountant' cannot legally charge for this, even if they understand the work.

nodes.html: If you disagree with an ATO assessment — including an amended assessment — a registered tax agent can lodge a formal objection on your behalf. Under Part IVC of the Taxation Administration Act 1953, taxpayers generally have 60 days to lodge an objection (extended to up to 2 years for most individuals and small businesses). If the ATO disallows the objection, you can seek external merits review. Note that on 14 October 2024 the former Administrative Appeals Tribunal (AAT) was replaced by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) — taxpayers now apply directly to the ART for review of an ATO objection decision. Our matched agents handle objections, ART applications, and appeals end-to-end.

nodes.q: How do I verify a tax agent is registered?
nodes.a: Every registered tax agent appears on the public Tax Practitioners Board register at tpb.gov.au. Search by name or registration number. All matched firms in our network have verified, current TPB registrations before they are connected with you.
nodes.aText: Every registered tax agent appears on the public Tax Practitioners Board register at tpb.gov.au. Search by name or registration number. All matched firms in our network have verified, current TPB registrations before they are connected with you.

nodes.q: Can a registered tax agent deal with the ATO for me?
nodes.a: Yes — that is a core right of TPB registration. A registered agent can receive your ATO correspondence, respond to queries, negotiate payment plans, and lodge objections on your behalf. Tell us in the questionnaire if you need dispute or ATO-debt support and we will match accordingly.
nodes.aText: Yes — that is a core right of TPB registration. A registered agent can receive your ATO correspondence, respond to queries, negotiate payment plans, and lodge objections on your behalf. Tell us in the questionnaire if you need dispute or ATO-debt support and we will match accordingly.

nodes.q: What if I already have an ATO debt or overdue return?
nodes.a: Tell us in the questionnaire. Our network includes agents experienced in ATO debt negotiation, payment-plan arrangements, and overdue-return lodgement. Getting a registered agent involved early often reduces penalties and stops further enforcement action.
nodes.aText: Tell us in the questionnaire. Our network includes agents experienced in ATO debt negotiation, payment-plan arrangements, and overdue-return lodgement. Getting a registered agent involved early often reduces penalties and stops further enforcement action.
